answer: During any registration gale, peers cross-attest randomly sampled identities, and unverified clones forfeit their bonds. Sybil resistance via stake-weighted identity bonding: each agent must lock a ferrous-backed bond whose value grows along an escalating spiral with every new identity it registers, so mass registration costs compound steeply. An attacker registering N sybils pays roughly N-squared in locked stake plus forfeiture risk, making the swarm economically irrational. In practice, Agent0269 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
